claims.claim: For a binary pointer ensemble and any POVM, classical common-overlap decomposition yields I(X:Y)<=H(X) TV(P0,P1)<=H(X) D(rho0,rho1). Together with Holevo and explicit projective candidates this bounds unrestricted accessible information. In the registered dataset the TV bound did not tighten Holevo at tolerance, and attainable candidates improved Z information in 10670 of 25920 evaluations.
claims.limit: Finite specified binary ensembles, no claimed unrestricted POVM optimum or new general theorem; no native physical objectivity.

claims.claim: Exact disjoint packing from lower and upper fragment information bounds gives a certified cardinality interval. For H>1e-6 and 90% threshold, no two qualifying fragments are possible for either registered pointer in final plus81 xi1. All 18 attained two-fragment conditions are six native-repeat base81 contexts at three tags; one extra unresolved condition. System-Z has no possible two-fragment packing in any registered condition.
claims.limit: Finite conditional model, not a universal no-go. Lambda0 counterfactual uses harvested plus settings; repeated tags not independent contexts; degeneracy and success weights retained.
